_readme: Cockney isolated phonemes - HUMAN recordings, one consistent
reference voice. This manifest is production tooling only; it never ships
(tools/ is excluded from the deployed artifact). It is also the file
tools/prep_phonemes.py reads to know the order and the names, so a session
cannot be prepped without it.
Workflow: record each entry -> name the file <slug>.mp3 -> run
python3 tools/prep_phonemes.py <folder> --manifest tools/phoneme_manifest_cockney.json --out prepped/
python3 tools/import_phonemes.py prepped/ --dialect cockney --voice reference --dry-run
then again without --dry-run, listen at #audit, mark Good, export the
flags file and commit it. Nothing plays for a learner until the exact
dialect/voice/slug id is in APPROVED_PHONEMES.
General guidance: quiet room, consistent mic distance, no added vowel
after consonants, no trailing breath. A syllable demonstration must
sound like a syllable ON PURPOSE - it is labelled as one in the app.
Entry order follows docs/PHONEME_RECORDING_LIST.md, because
tools/prep_phonemes.py --split names files BY THIS ORDER when it cuts one
continuous take - recording in a different order misnames every clip.
Syllable-demo frame: /ɑː/ (PALM/BATH) - named directly in the spec's core
('Non-rhotic with broad BATH /ɑː/'), and long, open and unrounded, so it
neither rounds nor colours the consonant release. It sits outside the
diphthong shift and outside TH-fronting, h-dropping, glottalling and
L-vocalization, so the frame never competes with the consonant on show.
Cast a native broad London speaker (East End or an estuary town), not an
RP-trained actor dialling down - the diphthong shift and the glottal norm
have to be native, not performed.
The biggest booth risk is the four clips that fight the speaker's own
accent: /θ/ and /ð/ (life says [f] and [v]), /h/ (life drops it) and /l/
(life vocalizes to [o]). Brief these before the session, not mid-take.
Same conflict on t_syllable: the aCa frame puts /t/ between vowels,
exactly where Cockney glottals. Record a true [t] anyway - [ʔ] has its own
clip.
Keep every aCa frame vowel identical across the eleven syllable demos; the
frame must never become the lesson.
SHARE RULE. Most of these sounds are the same in every course, so one take
is recorded and copied into each. That is NOT safe for every entry: where an
accent's own published spec names a departure, that accent records its own.
Each entry carries "take": "shared" or "accent-specific" - never reuse
another course's file for an accent-specific one.
Accent-specific in Cockney (4): face_diphthong, price_diphthong, goat_diphthong, mouth_diphthong

entries.guidance: Controlled voiceless sustain /fff/, ~1s, no vowel either side. This is also the sound TH-fronting gives think [fɪŋk], which is why three and free merge.
Voiced labiodental sustain /vvv/, ~1s, buzz audible throughout. This is also the sound /ð/ fronts to in brother [ˈbrʌvə] - one target, not two.
True dental /θ/, sustained ~1s, tongue tip at the teeth, no added vowel. Record the phoneme, not the TH-fronted [f] of think [fɪŋk].
True voiced dental /ð/, sustained ~1s with buzz, no added vowel. Record the phoneme, not the [v] a broad speaker fronts it to, nor the [d] of function words.
Controlled voiceless sustain /sss/, ~1s. No vowel before or after.
Voiced sustain /zzz/, ~1s, buzz audible throughout. No added vowel.
Sustained /ʃʃʃ/, ~1s, lips slightly forward, groove steady. No vowel before or after.
Voiced sustain /ʒ/ as in measure, ~1s, buzz throughout. No added vowel and no slipping into /ʃ/.
Sustained voiceless breath /h/, ~1s of audible airflow, no vowel after it. Cockney drops /h/ in content words - that is taught in words, not here.
Hummed /mmm/, ~1s, lips closed the whole time. No vowel before or after.
Sustained /nnn/, ~1s, tongue tip on the ridge throughout. No vowel before or after.
Sustained velar /ŋ/, ~1s, nasal and steady. No /g/ release at the end and no added vowel.
Clear alveolar /l/, sustained ~1s, tongue tip on the ridge. No added vowel, and do not slide to [o] - L-vocalization of dark /l/ is taught in words.
Sustained approximant /r/ [ɹ], ~1s, no vowel before or after. No trill and no tap; the accent is non-rhotic, so this is the before-a-vowel /r/.
Steady lax /ɪ/ as in kit, ~0.7-1s at stable pitch. Do not drift toward /iː/ - the tense happY /i/ has its own clip.
Steady /e/ as in dress, ~0.7-1s. Keep it a pure monophthong - no glide of any kind, and no drift down toward TRAP /æ/.
Open short /æ/ as in trap, ~0.7-1s. Keep it clearly TRAP - do not raise it toward /e/, and do not broaden it to the London BATH /ɑː/.
entries.takeNote: Standard British records its own take of this sound; this one is the shared take

entries.guidance: Stressed /ʌ/ as in butter, ~0.7-1s - fuller and more energetic than schwa. Hold one position, no drift toward /ɒ/.
Short lax rounded /ʊ/ as in foot, ~0.7-1s. Light rounding only - do not lengthen or tense it into GOOSE /uː/.
Short rounded /ɒ/ as in lot, ~0.7-1s. Keep the lip rounding - the London skeleton has a rounded LOT; never unround it toward [ɑ].
Neutral unstressed schwa, short side of ~0.7s, low energy. Keep it colourless - the opening toward [ɐ] belongs to final -er in words, not here.
Tense but weak /i/ as in city, short side of ~0.7s, low energy. The /iː/ quality without its length - never stressed, never lengthened.
Tense long /iː/ as in fleece, ~1s, steady throughout. No onglide and no diphthongisation - one position from start to finish.
entries.takeNote: General Australian records its own take of this sound; this one is the shared take

entries.guidance: Long open back /ɑː/ as in bath, the broad London BATH vowel, ~1s. Non-rhotic - no r-colour, no r at the end. It is also the aCa frame vowel.
Long rounded /ɔː/ as in thought, ~1s with rounding held throughout. Non-rhotic - no r-colour, and no drift open toward /ɒ/.
Long rounded /uː/ as in goose, ~1s, rounding held throughout. One steady position - no glide, and no drift toward /ʊ/.
entries.takeNote: Standard British records its own take of this sound; this one is the shared take

entries.guidance: Long mid central /ɜː/ as in nurse, ~1s, steady and fully stressed - clearly longer and stronger than schwa. Non-rhotic, so no r-colour at all.
Long steady /ɛː/ as in fair, ~1s - one position, no glide, non-rhotic so no r. Keep it longer and opener than DRESS /e/ or the two clips merge.
Broad /eɪ/ spoken with the Cockney diphthong shift [æɪ]: start open near [æ], glide to [ɪ], ~1s. The whole journey - not an unshifted [eɪ].
entries.takeWhy: cockney core: the diphthong shift, FACE realized [æɪ]

entries.guidance: Broad /aɪ/ spoken with the shift [ɑɪ]: start open and further back, glide to [ɪ], ~1s. Audible journey - do not start front.
entries.takeWhy: cockney core: the diphthong shift, PRICE realized [ɑɪ]

entries.guidance: Broad /ɔɪ/, ~1s: rounded start gliding to [ɪ]. The shift the spec names is FACE, PRICE and GOAT, so hold CHOICE near its broad value.
Broad /əʊ/ spoken with the shift [æʊ]: start open and front near [æ], glide to [ʊ], ~1s. Do not start at schwa.
entries.takeWhy: cockney core: the diphthong shift, GOAT realized [æʊ]

entries.guidance: Cockney /aʊ/, ~1s: onset lower and backer than shifted GOAT [æʊ], gliding to [ʊ]. Lean toward the broad flattened [æː] quality but keep the glide.
entries.takeWhy: cockney common: MOUTH flattened toward a long [æː]

entries.guidance: Full centring glide /ɪə/, ~1s: start at /ɪ/ and land on schwa. Non-rhotic - no r at the end, and no smoothing to a long monophthong.
entries.takeNote: Standard British records its own take of this sound; this one is the shared take

entries.guidance: Full centring glide /ʊə/, ~1s: rounded /ʊ/ start landing on schwa. Non-rhotic - no r at the end, and do not collapse it into /ɔː/.
entries.takeNote: General Australian records its own take of this sound; this one is the shared take

entries.guidance: Syllable demo (stops and affricates cannot be sustained): a clean /ɑːpɑː/ - full closure and a crisp release, never a standalone 'puh'.
Syllable demo: /ɑːbɑː/ - voicing running right through the closure, then a clean release. No 'buh'.
Syllable demo: /ɑːtɑː/ with a true alveolar [t]. This clip is the phoneme /t/ itself - Cockney's [ʔ] between vowels has its own clip, so do not glottal here.
Syllable demo: /ɑːdɑː/ - a true alveolar /d/, voiced right through the closure, then a clean release. Never 'duh'.
Syllable demo: /ɑːkɑː/ - clean velar closure and release, no 'kuh'.
Syllable demo: /ɑːgɑː/ - voiced velar closure and release. No 'guh' and no trailing breath.
Syllable demo: /ɑːtʃɑː/ - a single affricate, closure running into friction, never 'chuh'. It is the sound of Cockney's coalesced tune [tʃuːn].
Syllable demo: /ɑːdʒɑː/ - one voiced affricate, not /d/ plus /ʒ/, never 'juh'. It is the sound of Cockney's coalesced duty [ˈdʒuːʔi].
Syllable demo: /ɑːwɑː/ - glide in and out through rounded lips, never a standalone 'wuh'.
Syllable demo: /ɑːjɑː/ - a free /j/ as in yes, never 'yuh'. Cockney fuses /j/ after /t d/ (tune [tʃuːn]); keep this one separate.
Syllable demo (a stop cannot be sustained): [ɑːʔɑː] - vocal folds close, a beat of silence, clean release. [ʔ] realizes /t/ here, it is not an extra phoneme.
